page: Amazon Web Services c6a.24xlarge is a compute-optimized instance built on the AWS Nitro System and powered by third-generation AMD EPYC 7R13 processors. Featuring an x86_64 architecture, the instance provides 96 vCPUs across 48 physical cores with simultaneous multithreading at a clock speed of up to 3.6 GHz. Memory is configured with 192.0 GB of DDR4 RAM running at 3 GHz, maintaining a 1:2 memory-to-vCPU ratio of 2.0 GB per vCPU. Hardware cryptographic acceleration is enabled via AES, VAES, and SHA extensions, although AVX-512 and AMX instructions are absent. Local storage is not bundled, requiring external network-attached EBS volumes for persistent storage, while baseline network bandwidth reaches 38 Gbps without complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark data reflects robust multi-threaded CPU throughput, positioning the instance in the top tier for multi-core stress-ng tests and Geekbench ray tracing. Encryption performance is similarly high, with PassMark CPU encryption metrics landing in the top tier. Memory bandwidth achieves strong results for small cached blocks, though larger uncached read and write operations perform within the middle tier. In application tests, the instance records strong results in Clang software compilation, PassMark database operations, and Redis SET workloads, while static web serving throughput and standard single-threaded compression run at average speeds.

Without included GPUs or onboard NVMe storage, the c6a.24xlarge focuses entirely on pure compute density and core parallelism. Its compute-optimized resource allocation delivers high multi-core throughput per provisioned resource. This configuration fits high-performance computing, distributed software compilation, batch processing, video rendering, and compute-intensive microservices.
description: Amazon Web Services c6a.24xlarge is a compute-optimized instance powered by a 3.6 GHz AMD EPYC 7R13 processor under the AWS Nitro hypervisor. Built on the x86_64 architecture, it delivers 96 vCPUs across 48 physical cores paired with 192.0 GB of DDR4 memory running at 3 GHz, representing a standard compute-focused 1:2 vCPU-to-memory ratio. It lacks dedicated GPUs and includes no local storage, relying on external network-attached volumes, while offering a 38 Gbps baseline network interface. Benchmark results indicate high multi-core capability, yielding top-tier scores in multi-core stress-ng tests and hardware encryption, alongside strong execution in software compilation and Redis operations. The c6a.24xlarge provides dense compute capacity suited for compute-heavy workloads such as distributed batch processing, parallel compilation pipelines, and CPU-driven scientific simulations.
